title: Cheers as murder charge dismissed for Queensland woman who helped terminally ill husband die
summary:
Kylie Ellina Truswell-Mobbs, 52, walks out of court after receiving suspended sentence over 2023 death of David Ronald Mobbs

  • Get our

blocks.text: A Queensland woman facing a potential life sentence after she gave her terminally ill husband a lethal cocktail of drugs has walked out of court to the sound of cheers.
Kylie Ellina Truswell-Mobbs, 52, pleaded not guilty to murder but guilty to assisting suicide in the supreme court in Brisbane on Monday.
Prosecutors had accepted the guilty plea over the death of former firefighter David Ronald Mobbs, 56, at the couple’s Alexandra Hills home in December 2023.
Mobbs was suffering from an aggressive form of motor neurone disease (MND).
Justice Tom Sullivan sentenced Truswell-Mobbs to a suspended jail term after accepting she had acted out of a sense of compassion.
As she left court, Truswell-Mobbs was cheered and hugged by family and supporters.
She said she was happy the court ordeal was over.
“It feels good,” Truswell-Mobbs told reporters. “[David] was beautiful. He will never be forgotten about.”
Truswell-Mobbs earlier cried and sobbed in the dock after Sullivan dismissed the murder charge.
“It was exceptionally difficult circumstances in which she found herself,” crown prosecutor Caroline Marco said.
Sullivan had heard that Mobbs’s once‑strong and fit body had been rapidly paralysed by the degenerative effects of MND soon after being diagnosed in April 2023.
Within months, he went from independent to being entirely bedridden. He was unable to walk or move without assistance, the court heard.
Mobbs had a terminal diagnosis and was likely eligible for voluntary assisted dying under legislation activated in early 2023.
But he had been told accessing it would take nine days or more, defence barrister Ruth O’Gorman told the court.

By 5 December 2023, he could no longer speak and was only communicating by blinking, making noises or using a letter board if someone lifted his hand.
Mobbs was also in pain and highly distressed due to losing the ability to use the toilet by himself.
“That night he begged to die,” O’Gorman said.
“There was nothing secret about it. It was done with full knowledge of her sons and number of carers.”
He died on 6 December 2023.
Sullivan said it was a challenging sentence, due to a lack of similar cases and Truswell-Mobbs having already spent 14 months in custody.
She was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment, suspended immediately due to time served.
